subsections.banner: TRANSFORMATIONS (chapter-style boxed banner, NO chapter number, starts mid-page)

chapter.note: The book prints TRANSFORMATIONS as a separate banner immediately after chapter 8's VSAQ run and restarts numbering at 1. Our bank holds both under one unit (mathematics unit 8), so both are indexed here and every question carries book_subsection.

questions.stem: Find the period of f(x) = tan 5x.
Find the period of f(x) = cos((4x + 9)/5).
Find the period of f(x) = |sin x|.
Find the period of tan(x + 4x + 9x + … + n²x).
questions.notes: Q2's three parts do NOT share one instruction — only i) is a period-of-this-function task; ii) and iii) each carry their own instruction, so they are emitted separately.

questions.stem: Find the sine function whose period is 2/3.
Find the cosine function whose period is 7.
Find the period of f(x) = cos(3x + 5) + 7.
Find the maximum and minimum values of f(x) = sin 2x − cos 2x over ℝ.
questions.notes: PRINTED DEFECT: Q4's sub-part list starts at ii) — no i) is printed anywhere under Q4.

questions.stem: Find the maximum and minimum values of f(x) = cos(x + π/3) + 2√2 sin(x + π/3) − 3 over ℝ.
Find the range of 13 cos x + 3√3 sin x − 4.
questions.notes: Star count uncertain: two stars are clear and a third may be clipped by the binding gutter. Q6 on the same page shows *** with its leading star at that same clipped position. Recorded low, not guessed upward.

questions.stem: Prove that (cos 9° + sin 9°)/(cos 9° − sin 9°) = cot 36°.
Find the value of sin² 82½° − sin² 22½°.
Find the value of cos² 112½° − sin² 52½°.
Find the value of sin² 52½° − sin² 22½°.
Prove that cot(π/20) · cot(3π/20) · cot(5π/20) · cot(7π/20) · cot(9π/20) = 1.
Prove that cos 12° + cos 84° + cos 132° + cos 156° = −1/2.
If cos θ + sin θ = √2 cos θ, prove that cos θ − sin θ = √2 sin θ.
If 3 sin θ + 4 cos θ = 5, find the value of 4 sin θ − 3 cos θ.
If sec θ + tan θ = 2/3, find sin θ and state the quadrant in which θ lies.
Find the value of cos 42° + cos 78° + cos 162°.
Find the value of sin 330° cos 120° + cos 210° sin 300°.
questions.notes: Stem printed at the foot of printed p.84; its solution runs onto p.85.

questions.stem: Find the value of tan 20° + tan 40° + √3 tan 20° tan 40°.
Prove that sin 50° − sin 70° + sin 10° = 0.
Eliminate θ from x = a cos³θ and y = b sin³θ.
If sin θ = 4/5 and θ is not in the first quadrant, find cos θ.
questions.notes: The book prints "first quasrant" — a typo for "first quadrant".

questions.stem: If cos θ = −5/13 and π/2 < θ < π, find sin 2θ.
Prove that tan α = sin 2α/(1 + cos 2α), and use it to obtain the values of tan 15° and tan 22½°.
For what values of x in the first quadrant is (2 tan x)/(1 − tan² x) positive?
If A, B, C are the angles of a triangle and none of them equals π/2, prove that tan A + tan B + tan C = tan A tan B tan C.
questions.notes: The book asks this identity TWICE — again as Q32 i) on printed p.89, there without the "none equals π/2" caveat.

questions.stem: If x = 2 sin θ/(1 + cos θ + sin θ), find the value of (1 − cos θ + sin θ)/(1 + sin θ).
Prove that cos 100° cos 40° + sin 100° sin 40° = 1/2.
If sin α = 1/√10, sin β = 1/√5 and α, β are acute, show that α + β = π/4.
Find the value of cos 48° · cos 12°.
questions.notes: The book's instruction word is "Solve", but the task is to evaluate the product.

questions.stem: Prove that 4(cos 66° + sin 84°) = √3 + √15.
Draw the graph of y = tan x on (−π/2, π/2).
Draw the graph of y = cos² x on (0, π).
Draw the graph of y = sin 2x on [−π/2, π/2].
If A, B, C, D are the angles of a cyclic quadrilateral, prove that (i) sin A − sin C = sin D − sin B and (ii) cos A + cos B + cos C + cos D = 0.
questions.notes: Kept as ONE object: a single instruction over a single setup — both identities follow from the same cyclic-quadrilateral condition.

questions.stem: Show that cos⁴α + 2cos²α(1 − 1/sec²α) = 1 − sin⁴α.
If A − B = 3π/4, show that (1 − tan A)(1 + tan B) = 2.
If A + B = π/4, prove that (a) (1 + tan A)(1 + tan B) = 2 and (b) (cot A − 1)(cot B − 1) = 2.
questions.notes: Lettered parts a) and b) share the one condition A + B = π/4, so they stay in one object.

questions.stem: If A, B, C are the angles of a triangle, prove that tan A + tan B + tan C = tan A tan B tan C.
questions.notes: Star sits on the question number (*32), not on the sub-part. Same identity as Q22 on printed p.86.

questions.stem: If A, B, C are the angles of a triangle, prove that cot A cot B + cot B cot C + cot C cot A = 1.
questions.notes: Star sits on the question number (*32), not on the sub-part.

questions.stem: Prove that cot(π/16) · cot(2π/16) · cot(3π/16) · … · cot(7π/16) = 1.
Show that cos⁴(π/8) + cos⁴(3π/8) + cos⁴(5π/8) + cos⁴(7π/8) = 3/2.
Show that cos²(π/8) + cos²(3π/8) + cos²(5π/8) + cos²(7π/8) = 2.
Show that sin⁴(π/8) + sin⁴(3π/8) + sin⁴(5π/8) + sin⁴(7π/8) = 3/2.
Prove that sin(π/5) sin(2π/5) sin(3π/5) sin(4π/5) = 5/16.
Prove that cos(π/11) cos(2π/11) cos(3π/11) cos(4π/11) cos(5π/11) = 1/32.
questions.notes: Star count uncertain — the left margin of scan 32 runs into the binding and only one star is legible; a second may be clipped. Recorded low.

questions.stem: Prove that cos(2π/7) · cos(4π/7) · cos(8π/7) = 1/8.
questions.notes: The stem prints a colon between the second and third factors where a product dot belongs.

questions.stem: If A ≠ nπ, n ∈ ℤ, prove that cos A cos 2A cos 4A cos 8A = sin 16A/(16 sin A), and deduce that cos(2π/15) cos(4π/15) cos(8π/15) cos(16π/15) = 1/16.
questions.notes: PRINTED DEFECT: the condition is set as "A ≠ nπ/n ∈ Z" — the slash stands where a comma belongs; A ≠ nπ, n ∈ ℤ is meant.

questions.stem: Prove that sin A sin(π/3 + A) sin(π/3 − A) = (1/4) sin 3A.
questions.notes: Stars sit on the question number (***39); the sub-parts carry none.

questions.stem: Prove that cos A cos(π/3 + A) cos(π/3 − A) = (1/4) cos 3A.
questions.notes: Stars sit on the question number (***39).

questions.stem: Prove that sin 20° sin 40° sin 60° sin 80° = 3/16.
questions.notes: Stars sit on the question number (***39).

questions.stem: Prove that cos(π/9) cos(2π/9) cos(3π/9) cos(4π/9) = 1/16.
questions.notes: Stars sit on the question number (***39).

questions.stem: Prove that (tan θ + sec θ − 1)/(tan θ − sec θ + 1) = (1 + sin θ)/cos θ.
Prove that tan 70° − tan 20° = tan 50°.
questions.notes: PRINTED DEFECT: as printed the identity is false. The correct statement is tan 70° − tan 20° = 2 tan 50°, and the book's own working ends at the factor 2.

questions.stem: Prove that 1/sin 10° − √3/cos 10° = 4.
Prove that √3 cosec 20° − sec 20° = 4.
If sin α/a = cos α/b, prove that a sin 2α + b cos 2α = b.
Prove that sin 18° = (√5 − 1)/4.
Prove that cos 36° = (√5 + 1)/4.
Prove that tan A + cot A = 2 cosec 2A.
Prove that cot A − tan A = 2 cot 2A.
If sin(α + β)/sin(α − β) = (a + b)/(a − b), prove that a tan β = b tan α.
If θ is not an integral multiple of π/2, prove that tan θ + 2 tan 2θ + 4 tan 4θ + 8 cot 8θ = cot θ.
questions.notes: Q47 prints both conditions in one preamble; each belongs to one sub-part, so the condition is split with the part it governs.

questions.stem: If 2A and 3A are not odd multiples of π/2, prove that tan 3A · tan 2A · tan A = tan 3A − tan 2A − tan A.
If 3A ≠ (2n + 1)π/2, prove that tan A tan(60° + A) tan(60° − A) = tan 3A, and find the value of tan 6° tan 42° tan 66° tan 78°.
If A, B, C are the angles of a triangle, prove that sin 2A + sin 2B + sin 2C = 4 sin A sin B sin C.
questions.notes: First question after the TRANSFORMATIONS banner, which starts mid-page on printed p.96 with no chapter number and carries only a Long Answer Questions block.

questions.stem: If A, B, C are the angles of a triangle, prove that sin 2A + sin 2B − sin 2C = 4 cos A cos B sin C.
If A, B, C are the angles of a triangle, prove that sin 2A − sin 2B + sin 2C = 4 cos A sin B cos C.
If A, B, C are the angles of a triangle, prove that cos 2A + cos 2B + cos 2C = −4 cos A cos B cos C − 1.
If A, B, C are the angles of a triangle, prove that cos 2A + cos 2B − cos 2C = 1 − 4 sin A sin B cos C.
If A, B, C are the angles of a triangle, prove that cos A + cos B + cos C = 1 + 4 sin(A/2) sin(B/2) sin(C/2).
If A, B, C are the angles of a triangle, prove that cos A + cos B − cos C = −1 + 4 cos(A/2) cos(B/2) sin(C/2).
If A + B + C = π, prove that cos²A + cos²B − cos²C = 1 − 2 sin A sin B cos C.
questions.notes: NUMBERING BREAK, recorded not renumbered: the "2." and "i)" labels sit in the binding gutter of scan 40 and are unreadable, so the stem reads as unnumbered. Star count unreadable for the same reason — recorded as null, not zero.

questions.stem: If A + B + C = π, prove that cos²(A/2) + cos²(B/2) + cos²(C/2) = 2[1 + sin(A/2) sin(B/2) sin(C/2)].
questions.notes: Printed without repeating the condition; it is inherited from the Q2 i) stem above it.

questions.stem: If A + B + C = π, show that cos(A/2) + cos(B/2) − cos(C/2) = 4 cos((π + A)/4) cos((π + B)/4) cos((π − C)/4).
questions.notes: NUMBERING BREAK, recorded not renumbered: "3. If A + B + C = π then show that" is printed and is followed immediately by ***ii). No i) identity is printed anywhere under Q3.

questions.stem: If A + B + C = π, show that sin(A/2) + sin(B/2) − sin(C/2) = −1 + 4 cos((π − A)/4) cos((π − B)/4) sin((π − C)/4).
If A, B, C are the angles of a triangle, prove that sin A + sin B + sin C = 4 cos(A/2) cos(B/2) cos(C/2).
If A + B + C = π/2, show that sin²A + sin²B + sin²C = 1 − 2 sin A sin B sin C.
If A + B + C = π/2, show that sin 2A + sin 2B + sin 2C = 4 cos A cos B cos C.
If A + B + C = π/2, prove that cos 2A + cos 2B + cos 2C = 1 + 4 sin A sin B sin C.
If A + B + C = 3π/2, prove that cos 2A + cos 2B + cos 2C = 1 − 4 sin A sin B sin C.
questions.notes: Q7 prints a sub-part label i) but no ii) follows — the run ends and Q8 begins.

questions.stem: If A + B + C = 2S, prove that sin(S − A) + sin(S − B) + sin C = 4 cos((S − A)/2) cos((S − B)/2) sin(C/2).
If A + B + C = 2S, prove that cos(S − A) + cos(S − B) + cos C = −1 + 4 cos((S − A)/2) cos((S − B)/2) cos(C/2).
If A + B + C = 0, prove that cos²A + cos²B + cos²C = 1 + 2 cos A cos B cos C.
questions.notes: The condition is set as "A + B + C = 0°" with a degree sign on the zero; Q10 sets the same condition without it.

questions.stem: If A + B + C = 0, prove that sin 2A + sin 2B + sin 2C = −4 sin A sin B sin C.
If α − β is not an odd multiple of π/2 and sin(α + β)/cos(α − β) = (1 − m)/(1 + m), prove that tan(π/4 − α) = m tan(π/4 + β).
If none of the denominators is zero, prove that ((cos A + cos B)/(sin A − sin B))ⁿ + ((sin A + sin B)/(cos A − cos B))ⁿ equals 2 cotⁿ((A − B)/2) when n is even and 0 when n is odd.
questions.notes: Last question of the chapter; its working closes on printed p.105 (scan 46).
